title: Fertility rate, total (births per woman)
citation: World Bank. World Development Indicators, indicator SP.DYN.TFRT.IN.
known_limitations: WB TFR is itself modelled for many low-income countries; differs from UN WPP by up to 0.2 births/woman. Aggregates (WLD, EAS) must be filtered out.
notes: Fully downloaded and parsed to processed/tfr_by_country_year.csv (16868 rows). The active prediction does not read it; it reads the hand-typed HISTORICAL_TFR and V12_ACTUAL_TFR_2024 in berm/data/countries.py instead.

title: Mobile cellular subscriptions (per 100 people)
citation: World Bank / ITU. World Telecommunication/ICT Indicators Database, indicator IT.CEL.SETS.P2.
known_limitations: SUBSCRIPTIONS ARE NOT PEOPLE AND NOT DOSE. Exceeds 100/100 in most countries from multi-SIM. No age, sex, body-proximity or duty-cycle information. Counts SIMs, not transmit time.
notes: 12861 rows in processed/mobile_by_country_year.csv. Read only by berm/stats/csli.py. The active exposure path uses the hardcoded power law in exposure/personal.py:tech_penetration_profile instead.

title: Individuals using the Internet (% of population)
citation: World Bank / ITU. World Telecommunication/ICT Indicators Database, indicator IT.NET.USER.ZS.
known_limitations: Definition of 'use' varies by national survey (last 3 months vs last 12 months). Not an RF quantity.
notes: 6812 rows. Used only in parse_all.generate_tech_diffusion to guess 3G/4G onset years for expansion countries.

title: Fixed broadband subscriptions (per 100 people)
citation: World Bank / ITU. World Telecommunication/ICT Indicators Database, indicator IT.NET.BBND.P2.
known_limitations: Fixed broadband is a wired quantity; its use as a Wi-Fi exposure proxy assumes an unmeasured router-per-subscription ratio.
notes: 5275 rows. Used only for 4G onset heuristics.

title: Urban population (% of total population)
citation: World Bank / UN WUP. World Development Indicators, indicator SP.URB.TOTL.IN.ZS.
known_limitations: National definitions of 'urban' are not comparable across countries. Does not give metro density or metro population share, which the ambient model needs.
notes: 17160 rows, parsed but never read by any module. COUNTRY_PARAMS.urban_frac and .metro_density are hand-typed instead.

title: Population, total
citation: World Bank. World Development Indicators, indicator SP.POP.TOTL.
geographic_coverage: 217 World Bank countries after metadata filter; WPP-only country/areas remain separately represented in the merged panel
known_limitations: Population revisions and national census quality vary; this is a denominator/covariate, not an RF or fertility measurement.
notes: Held in raw/world_bank/wb_global_2026-08-19/population.json. The global panel retains its source and missingness field-by-field; it does not impute unavailable values.

title: GDP per capita, PPP (current international $)
citation: World Bank. World Development Indicators, indicator NY.GDP.PCAP.PP.CD.
geographic_coverage: 217 World Bank countries after metadata filter; WPP-only country/areas remain separately represented in the merged panel
known_limitations: PPP series are estimated, periodically revised and not directly comparable to household income or fertility demand. Current international dollars add price-level/revision dependence.
notes: Held in raw/world_bank/wb_global_2026-08-19/gdp_ppp_per_capita.json. It is an observed source covariate only; a later hierarchical model must fit any coefficient within each training fold.

title: Contraceptive prevalence, any method (% of women ages 15-49)
citation: World Bank. World Development Indicators, indicator SP.DYN.CONU.ZS.
geographic_coverage: 217 World Bank countries after metadata filter; sparse observations for many countries
known_limitations: Survey timing, method definitions and married/all-women denominators vary; coverage is sparse and values must not be silently interpolated.
notes: Held in raw/world_bank/wb_global_2026-08-19/contraception_pct.json. The global panel preserves missingness and does not use it to alter the published Core-51 backtest.

title: COLOSS honey bee colony winter loss survey
citation: Gray A et al. 2020. Honey bee colony winter loss rates for 35 countries, winter 2018-2019. J Apic Res 59(5):744-751. doi:10.1080/00218839.2020.1797272
known_limitations: WINTER LOSS IS NOT A REPRODUCTIVE MEASURE. Mixed methodology: USA is BIP/AIA, EPILOBEE 2012-14 are unweighted apiary means. Only USA spans the full range; all other territories are confined to 2012-13..2019-20. The in-file winters_covered field lists 7 winters but the data block contains 19. No varroa, pathogen, pesticide, forage or weather covariates.
notes: 216 territory-winter records. Loaded by berm/stats/csli.py:load_bee_data. The 4 UK sub-national codes fail to join to the EMF proxy CSV, so 39/43 territories survive the join.

title: Decline in semen quality in a population of stud dogs
citation: Lea RG et al. 2016. Environmental chemicals impact dog semen quality in vitro and may be associated with a temporal decline in sperm motility and increased cryptorchidism. Sci Rep 6:31281. doi:10.1038/srep31281
geographic_coverage: Single site: Guide Dogs for the Blind Association, UK
known_limitations: SINGLE POPULATION, SINGLE BREEDING PROGRAMME, ONE COUNTRY. Values were digitized from Figure 1 and Figure 2a, not read from a data table; stated reading uncertainty is +-2-3 units. Values are model-estimated means from multilevel models, not raw observations. 1999-2001 are null because dogs were removed from the programme. NO RF MEASUREMENT ACCOMPANIES ANY POINT.
notes: ORPHANED: no code in the repository opens this file. berm/csli/species_data.py:DOG_ENDPOINTS restates the trends as hand-typed strings instead. Cannot support F1, F2 or F5, all of which require a regional or multi-country panel.

title: Country-level sperm concentration series reconstructed from meta-analysis
citation: Levine H et al. 2023. Temporal trends in sperm count: a systematic review and meta-regression analysis of samples collected globally in the 20th and 21st centuries. Hum Reprod Update 29(2):157-176. doi:10.1093/humupd/dmac035
license: Article CC-BY-NC; reconstruction is not the published data
known_limitations: NOT AN OBSERVED SERIES. The file's own notes state: country-level estimates reconstructed from regional/national studies cited in meta-analyses; direct country-level time series from the Levine meta are not publicly available in supplement. No CI, no n, no assay standardisation, no abstinence-time adjustment. Composition of contributing studies changes across years.
notes: 153 country-year points. Loaded by berm/stats/csli.py:load_sperm_data and used as the human endpoint in lag_invariance_test, which reports CV 1.414 on n=3 countries. To become OBSERVED this needs the Levine supplementary study-level table, which requires publisher access.

title: Pan-European Common Bird Monitoring Scheme indices
citation: PECBMS (Pan-European Common Bird Monitoring Scheme). pecbms.info. Annual updates.
known_limitations: An abundance index, not a reproductive measure. Irregular 2-6 year steps, not annual. Farmland and common-bird series are mixed in one table under a type field. The EUR aggregate has no EMF counterpart and drops from any join.
notes: 172 country-year points, 18 series. Loaded by berm/stats/csli.py:load_bird_data. Rosenberg KV et al. 2019 Science 366(6461):120-124 doi:10.1126/science.aaw1313 supplies the North American series.

title: Temporal trends in bull semen quality
citation: Wahl RL, Reif JS. Temporal trends in bull semen quality: a comparative model for human health? Environ Res. 2009;109(3):273-280.
known_limitations: NO NUMERIC SERIES IS PRESENT IN THE REPOSITORY. Only the citation and a qualitative trend string exist. Genetic selection and collection-protocol change over 1965-1995 are uncontrolled and are strong confounders of any bull trend.
notes: Required by falsification test F3 (bull as negative control). F3 cannot be computed. Needs the article's Table data or the underlying AI-station records.

title: Time trends, environmental factors and genetic basis of semen traits in Holstein bulls
citation: Karoui S et al. Time trends, environmental factors and genetic basis of semen traits collected in Holstein bulls under commercial conditions. Anim Reprod Sci. 2011;124(1-2):40-50.
known_limitations: NO NUMERIC SERIES IS PRESENT IN THE REPOSITORY. This study explicitly models genetic basis and environmental factors, which is exactly the confounding structure BERM must adjust for; using its headline trend without those covariates would be a misuse.

title: Boar semen quality time trends
citation: Hensel B et al. Anim Reprod Sci. 2025;286:108093.
known_limitations: NO DATA. data/sentinel/livestock_negative_control.json records data_available=false and 'Full text not accessible at extraction time'. CONFLICT: berm/csli/species_data.py:LIVESTOCK_DATA nevertheless attributes n_ejaculates=47757 over 1997-2019 to this citation, which the JSON does not support.
notes: Resolve the conflict between species_data.py and livestock_negative_control.json before this citation is used anywhere.

title: World Population Prospects 2024 Revision - age-specific fertility rates by 5-year age group
citation: United Nations, Department of Economic and Social Affairs, Population Division (2024). World Population Prospects 2024, Online Edition. Standard Projections, Fertility, CSV format.
geographic_coverage: 237 countries and areas (plus aggregates that the ingest filters out)
known_limitations: Estimates cover 1950-2023; 2024-2100 are medium-variant PROJECTIONS and are classified DERIVED, not OBSERVED. 95% prediction intervals exist only for projection years. WPP itself is a model: national estimates for countries with weak civil registration are reconstructed by UN DESA, not directly measured. The ingest keeps only the 15-49 groups, so 10-14 and 50-54 births are excluded; this shows up as a mean 0.39% residual against WPP's own TFR and is reported, never absorbed.
notes: Acquired 2026-08-19; replaces the hand-typed table as the ASFR basis. Ingested to processed/fertility_asfr_region_age_year.csv (250509 rows, contract-clean). The legacy berm/data/asfr.py:WPP_ASFR is retained untouched and diverges from this source by a mean 26.2% on implied TFR; see data-lineage-audit.md finding A-1.

title: World Population Prospects 2024 Revision - demographic indicators (medium variant)
citation: United Nations, Department of Economic and Social Affairs, Population Division (2024). World Population Prospects 2024, Online Edition. Standard Projections, Demographic Indicators, medium variant.
geographic_coverage: 237 countries and areas (plus aggregates that the ingest filters out)
known_limitations: Only TFR is ingested. Estimates cover 1950-2023; 2024-2100 are medium-variant projections classified DERIVED. WPP computes TFR from single-age rates, so it will never equal a 5-year-band sum exactly. No prediction interval is published in this file, so uncertainty columns are empty rather than invented.
notes: Ingested independently of the ASFR product precisely so that TFR = 5*sum(ASFR)/1000 is a test rather than a tautology. Ingested to processed/fertility_tfr_region_year.csv (35787 rows, contract-clean).

title: Pharmaceutical consumption - antidepressants
citation: OECD (2024). Health at a Glance / OECD Health Statistics, pharmaceutical consumption, antidepressants, DDD per 1000 inhabitants per day.
known_limitations: The hardcoded table in countries.py:ANTIDEPRESSANT_DDD includes non-OECD countries (China 5, India 3, Niger 0.5, Ethiopia 0.3) that OECD does not publish; those values have no traceable origin. Latest-available years are mixed across countries with no year column.
notes: Feeds only the DIAGNOSTIC_ONLY endogenous_ssri_model. Low priority for the active prediction, but the table currently mixes an OECD extract with untraceable additions and must not be cited as OECD as a whole.

title: BERM v17 internal scenario parameters
citation: BERM v17 parameter set, derived from L-BERM Wolfram reference v2026.08.18-v17-itu-integrated.
known_limitations: THESE ARE ASSUMPTIONS, NOT OBSERVATIONS. Every value carried under this source_id is a SCENARIO_PARAMETER and must be rendered as such in any interface, document or model output.
notes: Placeholder source for every hardcoded constant in v16.py, config.py, exposure/personal.py and the assumption-class tables of countries.py until each is replaced by a cited source. Individual entries are enumerated in parameter_registry.csv.
